finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete(u, a) but discards its boolean result, so the ownership/admin check never blocks the removal at line 23. Any authenticated non-admin user can delete any other user's account via DELETE /accounts/{id}.
finding.source: src/AccountService.java:20 deleteAccount(User u, long id) - id from the DELETE /accounts/{id} route (comment at line 19); u is the authenticated caller

trace.note: deleteAccount entry point takes caller User u and account id
canDelete(u, a) called; boolean result discarded, so no enforcement
canDelete returns u.admin() || a.ownerId() == u.id(), which returns false for non-owner non-admin
accounts.remove(id) executes unconditionally, deleting the victim's account

verdict.reason: deleteAccount at src/AccountService.java:22 discards the boolean from canDelete (defined at line 9-10), so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any caller who is not the owner or an admin; the attacker only needs to be an authenticated low-privilege user, assuming the route authenticates the caller, which the repo does not show.
